title: Capture wish file
description: Designed (docs/native/capture-split.md 4.4, #773), not implemented. `state/radio_wish.json`: the DESIRED state of radio capture and nothing else, written by the app (its only writer) with tmp + rename whenever it changes, read by capture on a `poke` and every 0.5 s. Level-triggered: a capture that starts alone runs what the file says. Nothing here needs an answer (that is a request on the socket) and nothing here is observed (that is the status file). Capture ignores a key it does not know; a file that is missing, unreadable or not an object leaves the last accepted wish running (never "everything off"); a part that fails validation is not applied, the rest is, and the status lists it under `refusals`. It carries no secret and no URL, and nothing capture executes: those come from the root-owned config, because the `sizeup` user can write this file. No key at any depth has `token`, `secret` or `password` in its name, in any case (`$defs/no-secrets`).

seq.description: A counter the app keeps in the file itself: the previous wish's plus 1. The status reports the `wish_seq` capture runs.

at.description: When the app wrote the file, Unix seconds.

mode.description: Which capture this wish is for: `service` or `shadow` (the shadow instance of the migration). Capture leaves a wish for a mode it does not know unapplied.

paths.title: Data directories
paths.description: Where capture keeps data. Data directories only: no program path. Each is absolute; one left out is the station default.

clips.description: The app's clips directory (same filesystem as the spool: audio moves by hard link).

state.description: The state directory (`radio.lock`, capture's own state files).

hub.title: The hub link, as the app sees it
hub.description: What the urgent senders need to know about the hub. No secret and no URL: capture reads the hub's URL from the root-owned config. A key named `url`, `hub_url` or `access_id` here (in any case) is not a wish a writer may send; capture ignores one and says so in `wish_problem`.

forward.description: The hub link is on. false (all-in-one, or the link switched off): capture writes urgent rows and sends nothing.

station.description: The station id the hub assigned (`StationLink.adopt`): the `station` of an urgent request.

caps.description: The hub's capability strings, as its state answer gave them. Capture sends only while `urgent` is among them.

items.title: One channel of the set
items.description: One `[[radio.channels]]` entry, as the app's config has it.

label.description: The channel's label: its name everywhere (jobs, sidecars, frames, the status).

kind.description: The channel's kind. Capture does not run a channel whose kind it does not know and reports a refusal.

gain_db.description: The tuner gain, dB; null for automatic.

device.description: The serial of the dongle the config pins the channel to; "" for none.

open_db.description: The quieting needed to open, dB, as configured. `squelch[label]`, when there, is what runs.

drop_db.description: End a transmission this far under its own level, dB; null for none.

hang_s.description: The squelch hang once a transmission has had tones or speech, seconds; null: by kind.

continue_s.description: How long after a close the carrier may come back and still be the same page, seconds; null: by kind.

keyups.description: The key-up cutting mode, as configured; "" for none.

split_s.description: Key-ups: the shortest gap that cuts, seconds; 0 for the default.

jump_db.description: Key-ups: the level jump that cuts, dB; null for the default.

schedule.description: Airband (#260): the frequency by the time of day, as [minute of the local day, MHz] in time order; [] for `mhz` all day.

also.description: Airband (#275): other frequencies on the same dongle, as [MHz, from, until, label], from and until in minutes of the local day or null; [] for none.

record.description: false: nothing is kept of this channel. Its sidecars carry ids, levels and the alarm, with `audio` null.

airband.title: Airband settings
airband.description: The owner rule for a frequency two dongles hear (`config.airband_owner` today) belongs here too; the design does not name its key, so it is not typed.

multichannel.description: Receive a dongle's `also` frequencies at once through the channelizer (#275).

squelch.description: The squelch values to run, by channel label, already fitted by the app. Applied live, no restart.

open_db.description: The squelch opens at this much quieting, dB.

close_db.description: The squelch closes below this much quieting, dB.

tones.title: The tone plan
tones.description: For the live page: the names a pair shows, and which names are ours.

items.title: One pair of the plan
items.description: A tone pair and who it pages.

ours.description: The names that are this department's own.

aliases.description: {radio id: name}: the alias an alarm's `unit` gets.

dongles.title: Dongles
dongles.description: What each dongle should do, as people chose it. What capture decides itself (auto-assigned jobs, stand-ins, dongles out for no audio, loans) is not here: it is in the status.

jobs.description: {serial: the job that dongle should run}. A job whose dongle another app holds, or that is parked, is no error: it shows as `held`, `shed` or `waiting`.

job.description: A channel's label, the P25 job, a system job, or `Off`.

by.description: Who chose it. `person` here: what auto-assign decides is capture's own.

items.title: One antenna group
items.description: An antenna group as saved (`groups.parse`'s shape), parks included.

sdrs.description: The serials of its dongles, in order.

jobs.description: Its jobs, the most important first.

parked.description: The jobs of the group a person parked; [] or absent for none.

reserved.title: Reserved dongles
reserved.description: Serials set aside for other decoders: never given a job.

adsb.description: The ADS-B decoder's dongle, a serial; "" for none.

ais.description: The AIS decoder's dongle, a serial; "" for none.

listed.description: The serials the config lists (`[radio] sdrs`); [] with `auto`.

auto.description: Use whatever dongles are plugged in (`[radio] sdrs = "auto"`).

order.description: The order auto-assign hands jobs out in (`[radio] auto_assign_order`).

ignore.description: Serials never shown or used (`[radio] sdr_ignore`).

start_mode.description: What a shared dongle does at startup (`[radio] start_mode`); "" for none.

p25.title: P25
p25.description: The county recorder and each system's directory, name, label, sources and jobs, and the talkgroup labels and unit aliases for `parse_call`. The design names only `talkgroups`; the rest is not typed here.

talkgroups.description: {system short name: {talkgroup number as decimal digits: facts}}: what the reception test needs to know of a talkgroup, resolved by the app.

additionalProperties.title: One talkgroup's facts
additionalProperties.description: Resolved by the app from its Settings.

metrics.description: Sample the `floor` and `cc` signal records (spool items of kind `metrics`).

spool.title: Spool bounds
spool.description: The spool's bounds with their defaults (contracts/capture/spool.md).

max_age_h.description: Unacknowledged items older than this lose their audio, hours. Default 12.

max_bytes.description: The spool's size bound, bytes. Default 2147483648.

max_items.description: Sidecars go only past this many items. Default 50000.

min_free_bytes.description: The free-space reserve of the spool's filesystem, bytes: under it capture publishes sidecars without audio. Default 268435456.

sync_s.description: How often what was published is synced to disk, seconds. Default 5.

no-secrets.title: No secret at any depth
no-secrets.description: No key of this object, or of any object or list inside it, is named like a secret: `token`, `secret` or `password` anywhere in the name, in any case.
